misconceptions: Mistaking evidence-seeking for accusations of selfishness

semantic_axes.description: Automatic selfish-motive attribution versus open-minded questioning

edges.boundary_rule: A cynic assumes people act from selfish motives rather than genuine goodness; a skeptic questions whether claims are true without presuming bad motives.
clues_b: asks for proof without accusing anyone of selfishness
irrelevant_clues: asking questions, a serious face, previous disappointment

misconceptions.M2: Mistaking evidence-seeking for accusations of selfishness
misconceptions.M3: Assuming any doubt reveals distrust of all human motives

beats.text: Aaliyah insisted her classmate volunteered only to earn credit, never because he wanted to help.
beats.reason: The clue 'assumed volunteering concealed selfish reward' points to distrust of human goodness, not doubt pending evidence.

beats.text: When she learned there was no credit, she claimed he must be seeking attention instead.
beats.decisive_clue: replaced one self-serving motive with another
beats.reason: The detail 'replaced one self-serving motive with another' leaves distrust of human goodness as the better fit, not doubt pending evidence.

chains.feedback_short: Replaced one self-serving motive with another; cynic still fits best.
chains.feedback_deep: cynic means person who assumes supposedly good actions hide self-interest; skeptic means person who questions claims or demands sound evidence. The first clue is "assumed volunteering concealed selfish reward"; the next is "replaced one self-serving motive with another". A skeptic asks for evidence; a cynic assumes self-interest.
